findings.title: Webhook callback URL can target the internal network
findings.description: validate_callback_url() only checks that the URL parses and uses http or https before Celery workers POST payment events to it. A customer can register an internal address and make the workers send requests to internal admin services and the cloud metadata endpoint.

findings.cweName: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
findings.title: No lockout or throttling on API login
findings.description: LoginView accepts unlimited password attempts per account and per IP address. Finance users' accounts can be brute-forced or targeted with credential stuffing.

findings.title: Bank feed files parsed with unsafe yaml.load
findings.description: parse_feed() loads customer-uploaded bank feed files with yaml.load and the full loader. A crafted feed file can instantiate arbitrary Python objects in the Celery worker that processes imports, which leads to code execution.

findings.title: Outdated cryptography package with published advisories
findings.description: requirements.txt pins cryptography 41.0.3, which has published advisories in its OpenSSL bindings. The package signs the payout files sent to partner banks.

findings.title: API tokens never expire
findings.description: REST framework tokens are issued without an expiry and are not rotated on password change, so a leaked token grants indefinite access to payment data.

findings.cweName: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
findings.title: Full bank account numbers returned by the payout API
findings.description: PayoutSerializer includes the full destination account and routing numbers instead of the last four digits. Any user with read access to payouts can collect supplier bank details.

findings.title: CSRF protection disabled on the legacy export form
findings.description: The legacy CSV export view is decorated with csrf_exempt. A malicious page can trigger a full ledger export for a logged-in finance user.

findings.cweName: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
findings.title: CORS allows all origins with credentials
findings.description: CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS is True together with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS, so any website can make authenticated requests to the API from a signed-in user's browser.

findings.cweName: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
findings.title: Payout file checksums use MD5
findings.description: Payout batch files sent to the bank are integrity-checked with MD5, which is no longer collision resistant. A tampered file could keep a matching checksum.
